meaning_en: Having a keen, practical ability to judge situations and make good decisions.
meaning_es: Con una aguda y práctica capacidad para valorar situaciones y tomar buenas decisiones.
collocation: a sagacious observer
note: Implies wisdom grounded in experience, not just intelligence; suits leaders, advisors, or veteran professionals.

examples.en: The sagacious investor had foreseen the market correction months before it happened.
examples.es: El sagaz inversor había previsto la corrección del mercado meses antes de que ocurriera.

examples.en: Her sagacious reading of the room prevented a confrontation before it could start.
examples.es: Su sagaz lectura del ambiente evitó un enfrentamiento antes de que pudiera producirse.

meaning_en: Most noticeable or important; standing out clearly from the surrounding context.
meaning_es: Lo más destacado o importante; que sobresale claramente del contexto que lo rodea.
collocation: a salient point, the salient features
note: Common in academic and professional writing; pairs well with 'point', 'feature', or 'detail'.

examples.en: The report buried its most salient finding in a footnote on page forty.
examples.es: El informe escondía su hallazgo más relevante en una nota a pie de página en la cuarenta.

examples.en: She asked the panel to focus on the salient differences between the two proposals.
examples.es: Pidió al panel que se centrara en las diferencias fundamentales entre las dos propuestas.

meaning_en: Optimistic, especially in a difficult situation; sometimes implying overconfidence.
meaning_es: Optimista, especialmente en situaciones difíciles; a veces con cierta connotación de exceso de confianza.
collocation: sanguine about the outcome
note: Can carry a hint of naivety; saying someone is 'too sanguine' suggests their optimism isn't well-founded.

examples.en: She remained sanguine about the project's chances despite the funding cuts.
examples.es: Se mantuvo optimista sobre las posibilidades del proyecto a pesar de los recortes de financiación.

examples.en: Critics accused the government of being sanguine about risks it should have taken more seriously.
examples.es: Los críticos acusaron al gobierno de ser demasiado optimista respecto a riesgos que debería haber tomado más en serio.

meaning_en: Grimly mocking or cynical; humour that has an edge of contempt or bitterness.
meaning_es: Burlonamente cínico o amargo; humor con un trasfondo de desprecio o amargura.
collocation: a sardonic smile, a sardonic remark
note: Describes a dry, knowing attitude rather than open ridicule; the tone is detached and slightly superior.

examples.en: He gave a sardonic smile when they announced the 'award' was unpaid.
examples.es: Esbozó una sonrisa sardónica cuando anunciaron que el 'premio' no era remunerado.

examples.en: Her sardonic commentary on office life made her newsletter a cult favourite.
examples.es: Su sardónico comentario sobre la vida en la oficina convirtió su boletín en objeto de culto.

meaning_en: Careful to do what is right and honest; paying close attention to detail and correctness.
meaning_es: Cuidadoso en actuar de manera correcta y honesta; muy atento a los detalles y a la exactitud.
collocation: scrupulous attention to detail
note: Can describe both moral integrity and methodical thoroughness; context usually clarifies which is meant.

examples.en: The auditor was scrupulous in documenting every discrepancy, no matter how minor.
examples.es: El auditor fue escrupuloso al documentar cada discrepancia, por pequeña que fuera.

examples.en: She was scrupulous about crediting everyone who contributed to the research.
examples.es: Fue escrupulosa a la hora de dar crédito a todas las personas que habían contribuido a la investigación.

meaning_en: A happy and unexpected discovery made while not specifically looking for it.
meaning_es: Un descubrimiento feliz e inesperado hecho sin buscarlo específicamente.
collocation: pure serendipity, an act of serendipity
note: Often romanticised; used in both casual storytelling and scientific contexts when chance leads to discovery.

examples.en: It was pure serendipity that they sat next to each other on the delayed flight.
examples.es: Fue pura casualidad afortunada que se sentaran juntos en el vuelo retrasado.

examples.en: Many of the lab's most important findings came about through serendipity rather than design.
examples.es: Muchos de los hallazgos más importantes del laboratorio surgieron por casualidad y no por diseño.

meaning_en: Showing eager care and concern for someone's wellbeing or comfort.
meaning_es: Que muestra un cuidado y una preocupación solícitos por el bienestar o la comodidad de alguien.
collocation: solicitous of her comfort
note: Has a slightly old-fashioned feel; can sound attentive or even fussy depending on degree.

examples.en: The host was solicitous throughout the dinner, refilling glasses before anyone asked.
examples.es: El anfitrión estuvo muy atento durante toda la cena, rellenando las copas antes de que nadie lo pidiera.

examples.en: Her manager called daily, solicitous about her recovery after the surgery.
examples.es: Su jefe llamaba a diario, preocupado por su recuperación tras la operación.

meaning_en: Not genuine or true; based on false reasoning or faulty evidence.
meaning_es: No auténtico ni verdadero; basado en un razonamiento falso o en evidencias poco fiables.
collocation: a spurious argument, spurious claims
note: Useful for calling out arguments that look plausible but don't hold up; implies the flaw is in the logic or source.

examples.en: The report drew spurious conclusions by conflating two unrelated data sets.
examples.es: El informe llegó a conclusiones espurias al confundir dos conjuntos de datos no relacionados.

examples.en: His alibi turned out to be spurious — the timestamps on the photos told a different story.
examples.es: Su coartada resultó ser falsa: las marcas de tiempo de las fotos contaban otra historia.

meaning_en: Settled and respectable but dull and unadventurous; resistant to change.
meaning_es: Asentado y respetable pero aburrido y poco aventurero; reacio al cambio.
collocation: a staid institution, a staid image
note: Often applied to institutions, industries, or people seen as overly cautious or conventional; not a compliment.

examples.en: The staid accounting firm surprised everyone by rebranding with a bold new identity.
examples.es: La anticuada firma contable sorprendió a todos al renovar su imagen con una identidad moderna y atrevida.

examples.en: Critics found the exhibition staid compared to the provocative work the artist had shown a decade earlier.
examples.es: Los críticos encontraron la exposición sosa en comparación con la obra provocadora que el artista había mostrado una década antes.

meaning_en: Resolutely firm and unwavering in purpose, loyalty, or belief.
meaning_es: Firme e inquebrantable en propósitos, lealtades o convicciones.
collocation: steadfast in her belief, a steadfast ally
note: Positive in tone; conveys reliability under pressure rather than mere stubbornness.

examples.en: He remained steadfast in his refusal to name his sources, even under legal pressure.
examples.es: Se mantuvo firme en su negativa a revelar sus fuentes, incluso bajo presión legal.

examples.en: The community's steadfast support kept the shelter open through years of budget threats.
examples.es: El inquebrantable apoyo de la comunidad mantuvo el refugio abierto durante años de recortes presupuestarios.

meaning_en: Enduring pain or hardship without showing one's feelings or complaining.
meaning_es: Que soporta el dolor o las dificultades sin mostrar sus sentimientos ni quejarse.
collocation: stoic endurance, stoic about the diagnosis
note: Can imply admirable self-discipline or, critically, an unhelpful suppression of emotion — context sets the tone.

examples.en: She was characteristically stoic when told the treatment had failed.
examples.es: Fue característicamente estoica cuando le dijeron que el tratamiento había fallado.

examples.en: His stoic acceptance of the setbacks earned him the respect of younger colleagues.
examples.es: Su estoica aceptación de los contratiempos le ganó el respeto de sus colegas más jóvenes.

meaning_en: Strict, precise, and demanding; leaving little room for deviation.
meaning_es: Estricto, preciso y exigente; que deja poco margen para desviaciones.
collocation: stringent regulations, stringent tests
note: Often used in regulatory, legal, or safety contexts; implies rigour rather than harshness for its own sake.

examples.en: The drug required stringent clinical trials before it could be approved for public use.
examples.es: El medicamento requirió rigurosos ensayos clínicos antes de poder ser aprobado para uso público.

examples.en: Stringent data-protection rules forced the company to overhaul its entire storage system.
examples.es: Estrictas normas de protección de datos obligaron a la empresa a revisar todo su sistema de almacenamiento.

meaning_en: Expressed briefly and clearly, without unnecessary words.
meaning_es: Expresado de forma breve y clara, sin palabras innecesarias.
collocation: a succinct summary, put it succinctly
note: A compliment in most professional contexts; implies the speaker has thought carefully before speaking.

examples.en: Her three-line email was more succinct than any of the hour-long meetings it replaced.
examples.es: Su correo de tres líneas fue más conciso que cualquiera de las reuniones de una hora que sustituyó.

examples.en: The professor praised the essay for being succinct without sacrificing depth.
examples.es: El profesor elogió el ensayo por ser conciso sin sacrificar la profundidad.

meaning_en: Done secretly, especially because it would not be approved of if noticed.
meaning_es: Hecho en secreto, sobre todo porque no sería aprobado si se descubriera.
collocation: a surreptitious glance, surreptitious recording
note: Used for covert actions large and small; the key quality is secrecy, not trivialness.

examples.en: She took a surreptitious look at her phone under the table during the lecture.
examples.es: Echó un vistazo furtivo al móvil bajo la mesa durante la conferencia.

examples.en: The journalist made surreptitious notes throughout the off-the-record briefing.
examples.es: El periodista tomó notas a escondidas durante toda la sesión informativa off the record.

meaning_en: A person who flatters important people to gain personal advantage.
meaning_es: Persona que adula a personas influyentes para obtener beneficios personales.
collocation: surrounded by sycophants
note: Used critically; the implication is insincerity — the flattery is calculated, not genuine.

examples.en: The CEO was so surrounded by sycophants that no one dared tell her the product was failing.
examples.es: La directora estaba tan rodeada de aduladores que nadie se atrevía a decirle que el producto estaba fracasando.

examples.en: He was a gifted engineer but a shameless sycophant who always agreed with whoever was senior.
examples.es: Era un ingeniero brillante pero un descarado adulador que siempre daba la razón a quien tuviera más rango.

meaning_en: Making a show of being morally superior; self-righteously pious.
meaning_es: Que alardea de superioridad moral; que se cree moralmente superior a los demás.
collocation: a sanctimonious tone, sanctimonious lectures
note: Strongly critical; the target is performative virtue rather than genuine ethics.

examples.en: His sanctimonious speech about plastic straws landed badly given his company's record.
examples.es: Su discurso mojigato sobre las pajitas de plástico cayó muy mal teniendo en cuenta el historial de su empresa.

examples.en: She delivered every piece of feedback with a sanctimonious air that made people dread her reviews.
examples.es: Transmitía cada comentario con un aire de superioridad moral que hacía que la gente temiera sus evaluaciones.

meaning_en: Appearing reasonable or valid at first glance but actually flawed or misleading.
meaning_es: Que parece razonable o válido a primera vista, pero que en realidad es erróneo o engañoso.
collocation: a specious argument, specious reasoning
note: The flaw may be in the logic, the evidence, or the framing — what matters is the plausible surface.

examples.en: The lawyer's specious argument relied on a technicality that the judge quickly saw through.
examples.es: El argumento especioso del abogado se apoyaba en un tecnicismo que el juez descubrió enseguida.

examples.en: The report made a specious case for the merger by cherry-picking favourable statistics.
examples.es: El informe presentó una justificación especiosa de la fusión eligiendo a dedo las estadísticas favorables.

meaning_en: Bad-tempered and resentful; silently gloomy and uncooperative.
meaning_es: Malhumorado y resentido; hosco y poco colaborador en silencio.
collocation: a sullen silence, a sullen teenager
note: Implies withdrawn hostility rather than active anger; often describes facial expression or atmosphere.

examples.en: He sat in sullen silence while his parents discussed what had gone wrong.
examples.es: Permaneció en un hosco silencio mientras sus padres hablaban de lo que había salido mal.

examples.en: A sullen mood hung over the office after the redundancy announcements.
examples.es: Un ambiente sombrío y resentido se cernió sobre la oficina tras los anuncios de despidos.

meaning_en: Dark or dull in colour or tone; serious, grave, and lacking cheerfulness.
meaning_es: Oscuro o apagado en color o tono; serio, grave y sin alegría.
collocation: a somber mood, a somber occasion
note: Can describe physical appearance or emotional atmosphere; often fits memorials, funerals, or difficult news.

examples.en: The prime minister addressed the nation in a somber tone after the disaster.
examples.es: El primer ministro se dirigió a la nación en un tono sombrío tras la catástrofe.

examples.en: The film's somber palette of greys and blues matched its themes of loss.
examples.es: La paleta sombría de grises y azules de la película concordaba con sus temas de pérdida.

meaning_en: Behaving as though one is superior to others; dismissively condescending.
meaning_es: Que se comporta como si fuera superior a los demás; condescendiente y desdeñoso.
collocation: a supercilious manner, a supercilious look
note: Implies the attitude is visible in behaviour — a raised eyebrow, a sigh, or a dismissive tone.

examples.en: The sommelier's supercilious smile made them feel foolish for ordering the house wine.
examples.es: La sonrisa altanera del sumiller les hizo sentirse tontos por haber pedido el vino de la casa.

examples.en: She described the consultant as supercilious — he spoke to the staff as if they were children.
examples.es: Describió al consultor como altanero: hablaba al personal como si fueran niños.

meaning_en: Giving the impression that something harmful or evil is present or intended.
meaning_es: Que da la impresión de que algo dañino o malévolo está presente o se pretende.
collocation: a sinister motive, a sinister figure
note: Works for both atmosphere and explicit menace; the threat is often implied rather than stated outright.

examples.en: There was something sinister about the way the man lingered outside the building every evening.
examples.es: Había algo siniestro en la forma en que el hombre merodeaba cada tarde frente al edificio.

examples.en: Investigators uncovered a sinister pattern behind what had appeared to be random accidents.
examples.es: Los investigadores descubrieron un patrón siniestro detrás de lo que parecían ser accidentes fortuitos.

meaning_en: Comfort or consolation in a time of distress or sadness.
meaning_es: Consuelo o alivio en un momento de angustia o tristeza.
collocation: find solace in, take solace from
note: Usually used with 'find' or 'take'; can describe a person, activity, or place that brings comfort.

examples.en: After the funeral, she found solace in long walks along the coastal path.
examples.es: Después del funeral, encontró consuelo en largos paseos por el sendero costero.

examples.en: He took solace in the fact that she had not been alone at the end.
examples.es: Se consoló con el hecho de que ella no había estado sola al final.

meaning_en: Involving immoral or dishonourable behaviour; dirty and unpleasant.
meaning_es: Que implica un comportamiento inmoral o deshonroso; sucio y desagradable.
collocation: a sordid affair, the sordid details
note: Often used in tabloid-style contexts for scandals; can also describe physical environments of poverty or neglect.

examples.en: The politician resigned after a sordid scandal involving misappropriated campaign funds.
examples.es: El político dimitió tras un sórdido escándalo que involucraba malversación de fondos electorales.

examples.en: The documentary exposed the sordid conditions in the city's unlicensed care homes.
examples.es: El documental denunció las sórdidas condiciones de las residencias de ancianos sin licencia de la ciudad.

meaning_en: Clever but misleading argument intended to deceive rather than illuminate.
meaning_es: Argumento hábil pero engañoso destinado a confundir más que a aclarar.
collocation: a piece of sophistry, descend into sophistry
note: Implies intentional manipulation; more pointed than 'specious' in suggesting bad faith.

examples.en: The defence team's sophistry had the jury confused about a timeline that was actually straightforward.
examples.es: La sofistería del equipo defensor dejó al jurado confundido sobre una línea temporal que en realidad era sencilla.

examples.en: She called out the sophistry in his argument: the statistics were real but the conclusion they implied was not.
examples.es: Señaló la sofistería de su argumento: las estadísticas eran reales, pero la conclusión que insinuaban no lo era.

meaning_en: Making or having a harsh, grating sound; or, in tone, forcefully assertive to an unpleasant degree.
meaning_es: Que produce o tiene un sonido áspero y chirriante; o, en tono, enérgico hasta resultar desagradable.
collocation: a strident voice, strident criticism
note: Used for both literal noise and rhetorical style; implies the delivery undermines the message.

examples.en: Her strident opposition to every proposal made compromise almost impossible.
examples.es: Su estridente oposición a todas las propuestas hizo que el compromiso fuera casi imposible.

examples.en: The organisation's strident tone alienated potential allies who shared its underlying goals.
examples.es: El tono estridente de la organización alejó a posibles aliados que compartían sus objetivos de fondo.

meaning_en: Calm, dependable, and not easily moved or excited; showing little emotion.
meaning_es: Sereno, fiable y difícil de perturbar o emocionar; que muestra poca emoción.
collocation: a stolid temperament, stolid reliability
note: Unlike 'stoic', 'stolid' suggests this is simply temperament rather than conscious self-discipline.

examples.en: The stolid night manager dealt with even the angriest guests with unruffled patience.
examples.es: El imperturbable encargado nocturno trataba incluso a los huéspedes más enfadados con serena paciencia.

examples.en: His stolid exterior hid a depth of feeling that rarely surfaced in conversation.
examples.es: Su exterior impasible escondía una profunda sensibilidad que raramente afloraba en la conversación.

meaning_en: Seeking to undermine or destabilise an established system, institution, or set of values.
meaning_es: Que busca socavar o desestabilizar un sistema, una institución o un conjunto de valores establecidos.
collocation: subversive ideas, a subversive comedian
note: Can be used approvingly in creative contexts (subversive art) or critically in political ones.

examples.en: Her subversive use of corporate imagery turned advertising's own tools against the brand.
examples.es: Su uso subversivo de la iconografía corporativa volvió las propias herramientas de la publicidad contra la marca.

examples.en: The government labelled the pamphlets subversive and ordered them confiscated.
examples.es: El gobierno tachó los panfletos de subversivos y ordenó su confiscación.

meaning_en: Deceit used to achieve a goal or avoid something unpleasant.
meaning_es: Engaño empleado para conseguir un objetivo o evitar algo desagradable.
collocation: resort to subterfuge, gain access by subterfuge
note: Implies a deliberate plan rather than a spontaneous lie; has a slightly theatrical, literary ring.

examples.en: The agent gained entry to the compound through a subterfuge involving a false identity.
examples.es: El agente accedió al recinto mediante un subterfugio que implicaba una identidad falsa.

examples.en: She suspected subterfuge when all three witnesses gave identical, rehearsed-sounding accounts.
examples.es: Sospechó que había subterfugio cuando los tres testigos dieron versiones idénticas que parecían ensayadas.

meaning_en: Distorted or biased so as to give a misleading impression; not straight or balanced.
meaning_es: Distorsionado o sesgado hasta dar una impresión engañosa; no recto ni equilibrado.
collocation: skewed data, skewed towards
note: Very common in data, journalism, and research contexts to flag unrepresentative samples or framing.

examples.en: The survey was skewed because it only reached people who were already engaged online.
examples.es: La encuesta estaba sesgada porque solo llegó a personas que ya participaban activamente en internet.

examples.en: Media coverage of the trial was heavily skewed toward sensationalism over fact.
examples.es: La cobertura mediática del juicio estuvo fuertemente sesgada hacia el sensacionalismo en detrimento de los hechos.

meaning_en: Sharply clear and plain, often in an unpleasant or bleak way; completely unadorned.
meaning_es: Claramente evidente y escueto, a menudo de forma desagradable o desoladora; completamente sin adornos.
collocation: in stark contrast, stark reality, a stark warning
note: Often used in 'stark contrast' or 'stark reminder'; suits landscapes, facts, or realisations that cut through illusion.

examples.en: The empty stadium stood in stark contrast to the scenes of celebration just weeks earlier.
examples.es: El estadio vacío contrastaba crudamente con las escenas de celebración de apenas unas semanas antes.

examples.en: The report was a stark reminder that progress on emissions had stalled.
examples.es: El informe fue un crudo recordatorio de que el progreso en las emisiones se había estancado.

meaning_en: Formal and dignified; conveying great seriousness or sincere commitment.
meaning_es: Formal y digno; que transmite gran seriedad o un compromiso sincero.
collocation: a solemn promise, a solemn occasion
note: Formal and grave in tone; pairs with oaths, ceremonies, and vows, though sincerity is not guaranteed.

examples.en: They stood in solemn silence as the names of the fallen were read aloud.
examples.es: Permanecieron en solemne silencio mientras se leían en voz alta los nombres de los caídos.

examples.en: She made a solemn promise to her daughter that she would be there for the graduation.
examples.es: Le hizo una solemne promesa a su hija de que estaría presente en la graduación.

meaning_en: Slow and gloomy in temperament; inclined toward gloom or sullenness.
meaning_es: De temperamento lento y melancólico; propenso a la tristeza o al mal humor.
collocation: a saturnine disposition, saturnine features
note: Has a literary and slightly archaic quality; useful for describing brooding characters in fiction.

examples.en: The saturnine barrister rarely smiled and seemed to find pleasure in proving others wrong.
examples.es: El taciturno abogado rara vez sonreía y parecía encontrar placer en demostrar que los demás estaban equivocados.

examples.en: His saturnine outlook made him a demanding colleague, though rarely a wrong one.
examples.es: Su actitud saturnina le hacía un compañero exigente, aunque raramente un compañero equivocado.

meaning_en: Easily made to feel sick, faint, or disgusted; reluctant to engage with unpleasant realities.
meaning_es: Que se marea, asquea o desmaya con facilidad; reacio a enfrentarse a realidades desagradables.
collocation: squeamish about blood, not for the squeamish
note: Used both literally (gore, medical procedures) and figuratively (uncomfortable truths or ethical grey areas).

examples.en: The documentary carries a content warning — it's not for the squeamish.
examples.es: El documental lleva una advertencia de contenido: no es apto para personas impresionables.

examples.en: She was too squeamish about offending sponsors to publish the most damning findings.
examples.es: Le daba demasiado reparo ofender a los patrocinadores como para publicar los hallazgos más comprometedores.

meaning_en: Having sharp judgement in practical matters, especially business; astute.
meaning_es: Con agudo criterio en asuntos prácticos, especialmente en los negocios; perspicaz.
collocation: a shrewd move, a shrewd negotiator
note: Usually a compliment; suggests the person sees angles others miss and acts on them effectively.

examples.en: It was a shrewd move to acquire the rival just before the market shifted in their favour.
examples.es: Fue una jugada hábil adquirir al rival justo antes de que el mercado se moviera a su favor.

examples.en: The agent was a shrewd reader of publishers — she knew exactly who would fight for the book.
examples.es: La agente era una perspicaz conocedora del mundo editorial: sabía exactamente quién lucharía por el libro.

meaning_en: Making critical or mocking remarks in an indirect or sly way.
meaning_es: Que hace comentarios críticos o burlescos de manera indirecta o solapada.
collocation: a snide remark, a snide comment
note: The indirectness is the defining feature — a snide remark says something cutting without committing to it openly.

examples.en: He made a snide comment about her promotion being down to 'other qualities'.
examples.es: Hizo un comentario solapado insinuando que su ascenso se debía a 'otras cualidades'.

examples.en: The review was full of snide jabs at the author's previous work without ever engaging the argument.
examples.es: La reseña estaba llena de pullitas solapadas sobre la obra anterior del autor sin llegar a debatir el argumento.

meaning_en: Nervous or easily startled; unpredictably jumpy or uncommitted.
meaning_es: Nervioso o que se asusta con facilidad; imprevisiblemente inquieto o poco comprometido.
collocation: skittish investors, a skittish horse
note: Works for animals, people, and markets; jitteriness may come from temperament or from outside pressure.

examples.en: Markets turned skittish after the central bank hinted at faster rate rises than expected.
examples.es: Los mercados se pusieron nerviosos después de que el banco central insinuara subidas de tipos más rápidas de lo previsto.

examples.en: The rescue dog was still skittish around strangers, but she had made enormous progress.
examples.es: La perra rescatada seguía asustándose con los desconocidos, aunque había avanzado muchísimo.

meaning_en: A mark of disgrace or strong disapproval associated with a particular condition or circumstance.
meaning_es: Una marca de deshonra o fuerte desaprobación asociada a una condición o circunstancia determinada.
collocation: the stigma around mental health, carry a stigma
note: Frequently used in public-health and social contexts; 'reduce the stigma' and 'attach a stigma' are common constructions.

examples.en: The campaign aimed to reduce the stigma around seeking help for addiction.
examples.es: La campaña pretendía reducir el estigma de pedir ayuda para superar una adicción.

examples.en: Bankruptcy still carries a social stigma in many professional circles.
examples.es: La quiebra sigue cargando un estigma social en muchos círculos profesionales.

meaning_en: Showy but cheap and of poor quality; unpleasantly sordid or squalid.
meaning_es: Llamativo pero barato y de mala calidad; desagradablemente sórdido o mísero.
collocation: a tawdry affair, tawdry decorations
note: Carries both aesthetic and moral senses; a tawdry affair is both sleazy and undignified.

examples.en: The whole tawdry episode was forgotten within a week once the next scandal broke.
examples.es: Todo el sórdido episodio cayó en el olvido en una semana, cuando estalló el siguiente escándalo.

examples.en: The once-glamorous hotel had become tawdry, its gilt fittings chipped and its carpets stained.
examples.es: El que fuera un hotel glamuroso se había vuelto chabacano: sus herrajes dorados estaban desportillados y las alfombras, manchadas.

meaning_en: Understood or implied without being directly stated; unspoken but recognised.
meaning_es: Entendido o sobreentendido sin ser expresado directamente; no dicho pero reconocido.
collocation: tacit approval, a tacit agreement
note: Used in legal, political, and interpersonal contexts; tacit approval may be inferred even without mutual awareness.

examples.en: By not objecting, the board gave tacit approval to the restructuring plan.
examples.es: Al no oponerse, el consejo dio su aprobación tácita al plan de reestructuración.

examples.en: There was a tacit understanding between them that certain subjects were simply off limits.
examples.es: Había entre ellos un entendimiento tácito de que ciertos temas estaban sencillamente fuera de los límites.

meaning_en: Reserved, saying very little; habitually reluctant to talk.
meaning_es: Reservado, que dice muy poco; habitualmente reacio a hablar.
collocation: a taciturn man, taciturn by nature
note: Describes a personality trait, not a momentary silence; a taciturn person may avoid speech rather than simply choose economy.

examples.en: He was taciturn in interviews, answering in monosyllables and never volunteering information.
examples.es: Era parco en las entrevistas: respondía con monosílabos y nunca aportaba información por iniciativa propia.

examples.en: The taciturn detective let the evidence speak and kept his own theories to himself.
examples.es: El taciturno detective dejaba que las pruebas hablasen y guardaba sus propias teorías para sí.

meaning_en: Only slightly related to the main subject; diverging from the central point.
meaning_es: Solo ligeramente relacionado con el tema principal; que se desvía del punto central.
collocation: tangential to the argument, a tangential point
note: Useful in academic and meeting contexts; implies the digression may be interesting but doesn't advance the argument.

examples.en: His comments about the company's history were interesting but tangential to the question of solvency.
examples.es: Sus comentarios sobre la historia de la empresa eran interesantes, pero tangenciales a la cuestión de la solvencia.

examples.en: The editor cut the tangential paragraphs on Victorian slang, however engaging they were.
examples.es: La editora suprimió los párrafos tangenciales sobre la jerga victoriana, por muy entretenidos que fueran.

meaning_en: Very weak or slight; lacking substance or sound basis.
meaning_es: Muy débil o tenue; que carece de sustancia o base sólida.
collocation: a tenuous link, tenuous evidence, a tenuous grasp
note: Common in academic and legal writing to flag weak reasoning; 'tenuous link' and 'tenuous grasp' are set phrases.

examples.en: The prosecution's case rested on tenuous circumstantial evidence and a single unreliable witness.
examples.es: El caso de la acusación se apoyaba en indicios circunstanciales endebles y un único testigo poco fiable.

examples.en: The connection between the two events was tenuous at best and the researchers acknowledged this.
examples.es: La conexión entre los dos hechos era tenue en el mejor de los casos, algo que los investigadores reconocieron.

meaning_en: Vigorous, incisive, and to the point in expression or thought.
meaning_es: Vigoroso, incisivo y directo en la expresión o el pensamiento.
collocation: trenchant criticism, a trenchant observer
note: Common in criticism and analysis; the sharpness may serve understanding or simply be cutting — context decides.

examples.en: Her trenchant analysis exposed flaws the development team had papered over for months.
examples.es: Su perspicaz análisis puso al descubierto fallos que el equipo de desarrollo había tapado durante meses.

examples.en: The trenchant editorial called the policy 'well-intentioned but catastrophically naive'.
examples.es: El incisivo editorial calificó la política de 'bien intencionada pero catastróficamente ingenua'.

meaning_en: Eager or quick to argue, fight, or be difficult; aggressively defiant.
meaning_es: Dispuesto o inclinado a discutir, pelear o mostrarse difícil; agresivamente desafiante.
collocation: a truculent witness, a truculent response
note: Implies combativeness that goes beyond confidence; suggests an itching for conflict rather than reasoned disagreement.

examples.en: The truculent witness turned every clarifying question into a confrontation.
examples.es: El agresivo testigo convirtió cada pregunta aclaratoria en un enfrentamiento.

examples.en: Management met the proposal with a truculent refusal to discuss any aspect of it.
examples.es: La dirección respondió a la propuesta con una negativa combativa a debatir ningún aspecto de ella.

meaning_en: Sparing with words, often to the point of seeming abrupt or unfriendly.
meaning_es: Parco en palabras, a menudo hasta el punto de parecer brusco o poco amigable.
collocation: a terse reply, a terse email
note: Similar to succinct but more likely to convey irritation or emotional distance than admirable brevity.

examples.en: He sent a terse reply — just two words — which the team interpreted as disapproval.
examples.es: Envió una escueta respuesta de solo dos palabras, que el equipo interpretó como desaprobación.

examples.en: Her terse instructions during the crisis left the interns unsure what to do next.
examples.es: Sus escuetas instrucciones durante la crisis dejaron a los becarios sin saber qué hacer a continuación.

meaning_en: A state of physical or mental sluggishness and inactivity; lethargy.
meaning_es: Estado de entorpecimiento físico o mental e inactividad; letargo.
collocation: fall into torpor, political torpor
note: More extreme than laziness; implies a loss of responsiveness, sometimes as a medical or institutional condition.

examples.en: The party had sunk into a torpor from which no new policy platform seemed able to rouse it.
examples.es: El partido había caído en un letargo del que ninguna nueva plataforma política parecía capaz de sacarlo.

examples.en: The long winter and isolation had produced a torpor she struggled to shake off come spring.
examples.es: El largo invierno y el aislamiento le habían provocado un letargo del que le costaba sacudirse al llegar la primavera.

meaning_en: Holding firm to something; persistent and determined in the face of difficulty.
meaning_es: Que se aferra con firmeza a algo; persistente y decidido ante las dificultades.
collocation: a tenacious campaigner, tenacious in her pursuit
note: Usually positive; can describe both people and beliefs, viruses, or plants in their refusal to yield.

examples.en: The tenacious journalist spent six years pursuing the story before finally breaking it.
examples.es: La tenaz periodista pasó seis años siguiendo la pista de la historia antes de publicarla por fin.

examples.en: Her tenacious grip on the contract terms eventually secured a far better deal for her client.
examples.es: Su tenaz insistencia en las condiciones del contrato consiguió a la larga un trato mucho mejor para su cliente.

meaning_en: A feeling of fear or apprehension about something that is about to happen.
meaning_es: Sentimiento de miedo o aprensión ante algo que está a punto de ocurrir.
collocation: with some trepidation, a sense of trepidation
note: Describes fear or apprehension before an event; 'with some trepidation' is a set construction.

examples.en: He opened the envelope with a trepidation he had not felt since his final exams.
examples.es: Abrió el sobre con una aprensión que no había sentido desde sus exámenes finales.

examples.en: The team approached the merger with trepidation, unsure what the new management would mean for them.
examples.es: El equipo afrontó la fusión con aprensión, sin saber qué significaría para ellos la nueva dirección.

meaning_en: Overused and lacking freshness; commonplace to the point of being uninteresting.
meaning_es: Trillado y carente de originalidad; tan común que resulta aburrido.
collocation: a trite observation, trite phrases
note: Describes ideas or language that were once meaningful but have been worn smooth by overuse.

examples.en: The speech was full of trite phrases about resilience that told the graduates nothing useful.
examples.es: El discurso estaba lleno de frases trilladas sobre la resiliencia que no decían nada útil a los graduados.

examples.en: She avoided the trite metaphors that plagued other lifestyle columns and wrote with precision instead.
examples.es: Evitaba las metáforas trilladas que plagaban otras columnas de estilo de vida y escribía con precisión.

meaning_en: Lukewarm; showing only half-hearted interest or enthusiasm.
meaning_es: Tibio; que muestra un interés o entusiasmo solo a medias.
collocation: tepid applause, a tepid response, tepid support
note: Works literally and figuratively; 'tepid applause' and 'tepid reception' are very common in reviews and politics.

examples.en: The announcement was met with tepid applause and a roomful of sceptical faces.
examples.es: El anuncio fue recibido con tibios aplausos y una sala llena de caras escépticas.

examples.en: The coalition's tepid support for the bill made its passage through the senate uncertain.
examples.es: El tibio apoyo de la coalición al proyecto de ley hizo incierta su aprobación en el senado.

meaning_en: Showing or suffering from nervousness or timidity; easily frightened.
meaning_es: Que muestra o padece nerviosismo o timidez; que se asusta con facilidad.
collocation: a timorous approach, timorous leadership
note: Slightly literary; often used of people seen as excessively cautious or nervous, and occasionally with sympathy.

examples.en: The committee's timorous approach to reform had frustrated campaigners for years.
examples.es: El timorato enfoque de la comisión ante la reforma había frustrado a los activistas durante años.

examples.en: He was too timorous to raise the issue with his manager, so it lingered for months.
examples.es: Era demasiado tímido para plantearle el problema a su jefe, así que la situación se prolongó durante meses.

meaning_en: To go beyond the limits set by a moral principle, rule, or law; to violate.
meaning_es: Sobrepasar los límites fijados por un principio moral, una norma o una ley; infringir.
collocation: transgress a boundary, transgress social norms
note: More emphatic than 'break'; implies crossing a line that has genuine moral or social weight.

examples.en: The ad campaign was pulled after it was judged to transgress standards of taste and decency.
examples.es: La campaña publicitaria fue retirada tras considerar que infringía los estándares de buen gusto y decencia.

examples.en: Her art deliberately transgressed gender norms to force viewers into uncomfortable territory.
examples.es: Su arte transgredía deliberadamente las normas de género para llevar a los espectadores a un terreno incómodo.

meaning_en: Present, appearing, or found everywhere at the same time.
meaning_es: Presente, que aparece o se encuentra en todas partes al mismo tiempo.
collocation: ubiquitous smartphones, the ubiquitous coffee shop
note: Sometimes used hyperbolically; works for cultural phenomena, technologies, and recurring types of people.

examples.en: The ubiquitous open-plan office became a symbol of an era that employers are now reconsidering.
examples.es: La omnipresente oficina de planta abierta se convirtió en símbolo de una era que los empleadores ahora reconsideran.

examples.en: By the late 2010s, QR codes had gone from a novelty to something ubiquitous.
examples.es: A finales de la década de 2010, los códigos QR habían pasado de ser una novedad a algo omnipresente.

meaning_en: Excessively eager to please in a way that feels insincere or oily.
meaning_es: Excesivamente complaciente de una forma que resulta insincera o empalagosa.
collocation: an unctuous manner, unctuous flattery
note: Describes insincerity that is visible in tone and manner; the comparison with sycophancy depends on context.

examples.en: The unctuous sales rep hovered at the table, complimenting every menu choice.
examples.es: El empalagoso representante de ventas rondaba la mesa elogiando cada elección del menú.

examples.en: His unctuous apology convinced nobody — it was too polished to be genuine.
examples.es: Su empalagosa disculpa no convenció a nadie: estaba demasiado elaborada para ser sincera.

meaning_en: Leaving no doubt; expressed or done in a way that is clear and completely decisive.
meaning_es: Que no deja lugar a dudas; expresado o realizado de forma clara y completamente decisiva.
collocation: an unequivocal denial, unequivocal support
note: Often used in politics and law to stress clarity; 'unequivocal' implies the speaker is not hedging.

examples.en: The board gave its unequivocal backing to the CEO despite pressure from shareholders.
examples.es: El consejo respaldó de forma inequívoca a la directora a pesar de la presión de los accionistas.

examples.en: His message to the press was unequivocal: there would be no extension to the deadline.
examples.es: Su mensaje a la prensa fue inequívoco: no habría ninguna prórroga del plazo.

meaning_en: Untidy or messy in appearance; not neat or well-maintained.
meaning_es: De aspecto descuidado o desordenado; sin arreglo ni mantenimiento.
collocation: unkempt hair, an unkempt garden
note: Applies to hair, clothing, gardens, and environments; not necessarily dirty, just neglected or dishevelled.

examples.en: He arrived looking unkempt, clearly having slept at his desk through the night.
examples.es: Llegó con un aspecto descuidado, visiblemente habiendo dormido en su escritorio durante toda la noche.

examples.en: The unkempt garden was a project she had promised herself to start every spring for five years.
examples.es: El jardín descuidado era un proyecto que llevaba cinco años prometiéndose empezar cada primavera.

meaning_en: Polished, confident, and at ease in social situations; courteous and refined.
meaning_es: Refinado, seguro de sí mismo y cómodo en situaciones sociales; cortés y cultivado.
collocation: an urbane manner, urbane charm
note: Has a faintly mid-century quality; suggests social fluency and sophistication, particularly in upper-class or cosmopolitan settings.

examples.en: The urbane diplomat navigated the gala with practised ease, charming every faction.
examples.es: El distinguido diplomático se movió por la gala con practicada soltura, cautivando a cada grupo.

examples.en: He was urbane and quick-witted in public, but his colleagues knew a sharper side of him.
examples.es: Era refinado y de ingenio rápido en público, pero sus colegas conocían su faceta más cortante.

meaning_en: Released from or not constrained by restriction; free to act or develop without limits.
meaning_es: Libre de restricciones o no limitado por ellas; con libertad para actuar o desarrollarse sin límites.
collocation: unfettered access, unfettered capitalism
note: Carries positive and negative connotations depending on context; 'unfettered press' is good; 'unfettered greed' is not.

examples.en: Researchers were given unfettered access to the archives for the first time in decades.
examples.es: Los investigadores tuvieron acceso sin restricciones a los archivos por primera vez en décadas.

examples.en: Critics argued that unfettered development had come at the cost of the coastline's character.
examples.es: Los críticos argumentaron que el desarrollo sin restricciones se había cobrado el carácter del litoral.

meaning_en: Without moral principles; willing to act dishonestly to get what one wants.
meaning_es: Sin escrúpulos morales; dispuesto a actuar de manera deshonesta para conseguir lo que uno quiere.
collocation: an unscrupulous operator, unscrupulous tactics
note: Implies calculated amorality rather than ignorance; the unscrupulous person knows the rules and ignores them.

examples.en: The landlord was unscrupulous enough to list the property on three platforms simultaneously.
examples.es: El propietario fue lo suficientemente poco escrupuloso como para publicar la propiedad en tres plataformas a la vez.

examples.en: Unscrupulous brokers had persuaded elderly clients to move savings into high-risk products.
examples.es: Agentes sin escrúpulos habían convencido a clientes mayores para trasladar sus ahorros a productos de alto riesgo.

meaning_en: Difficult to move, manage, or handle, due to size, shape, or complexity.
meaning_es: Difícil de mover, gestionar o manejar, por su tamaño, forma o complejidad.
collocation: an unwieldy bureaucracy, an unwieldy document
note: Applies to physical objects and abstract systems; 'unwieldy legislation' or 'unwieldy process' are common.

examples.en: The unwieldy codebase made onboarding new engineers a multi-month ordeal.
examples.es: La voluminosa base de código convertía la incorporación de nuevos ingenieros en una prueba de varios meses.

examples.en: A merger of five ministries produced an unwieldy department that struggled to make decisions.
examples.es: La fusión de cinco ministerios produjo un departamento inmanejable que tenía dificultades para tomar decisiones.

meaning_en: To waver between different opinions or actions; to be indecisive.
meaning_es: Vacilar entre distintas opiniones o acciones; ser indeciso.
collocation: vacillate between options, vacillate on policy
note: Implies a pattern of back-and-forth rather than a single moment of doubt; often used critically of leaders.

examples.en: The minister vacillated on the issue for so long that the window for action closed.
examples.es: El ministro vaciló tanto en el tema que la ventana de oportunidad para actuar se cerró.

examples.en: She vacillated between accepting the offer and staying in her current role until the deadline passed.
examples.es: Vaciló entre aceptar la oferta y quedarse en su puesto actual hasta que venció el plazo.

meaning_en: Offering nothing that stimulates, challenges, or interests; insipidly dull.
meaning_es: Que no ofrece nada estimulante, desafiante ni interesante; insulso y aburrido.
collocation: vapid conversation, vapid content
note: Dismissive; suggests total lack of substance rather than merely being boring. Harsher than 'bland'.

examples.en: The film's vapid dialogue made even its talented cast seem flat.
examples.es: Los vapuleados diálogos de la película hacían que incluso su talentoso reparto pareciera apagado.

examples.en: He sat through twenty minutes of vapid small talk before the meeting actually started.
examples.es: Aguantó veinte minutos de conversación trivial y vacua antes de que la reunión comenzara de verdad.

meaning_en: Expressing strong feeling or conviction with great passion and force.
meaning_es: Que expresa un sentimiento o convicción profunda con gran pasión y energía.
collocation: a vehement denial, vehement opposition
note: The feeling is strong and forceful; whether it reflects genuine inner conviction is not implied.

examples.en: She issued a vehement denial of the allegations before the interview had even properly begun.
examples.es: Emitió una vehemente negación de las acusaciones antes de que la entrevista hubiera ni siquiera empezado de verdad.

examples.en: His vehement opposition to the planning application united the otherwise divided neighbourhood.
examples.es: Su vehemente oposición a la solicitud urbanística unió al vecindario, por lo demás dividido.

meaning_en: Experienced through another person's actions rather than directly yourself.
meaning_es: Vivido a través de las acciones de otra persona y no de manera directa.
collocation: vicarious pleasure, vicarious thrill, live vicariously
note: Neutral; applies to pleasure, embarrassment, or pride felt through another person, not only longing.

examples.en: She got vicarious satisfaction from watching her students go on to build the careers she had imagined for herself.
examples.es: Sentía una satisfacción vicaria al ver a sus alumnos construir las carreras que ella había imaginado para sí misma.

examples.en: Travel blogs let readers live vicariously through adventures they may never take themselves.
examples.es: Los blogs de viajes permiten a los lectores vivir de manera vicaria aventuras que quizá nunca emprendan ellos mismos.

meaning_en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion; to show that a belief or action was correct.
meaning_es: Exonerar a alguien de culpa o sospecha; demostrar que una creencia o acción era correcta.
collocation: feel vindicated, vindicate a decision
note: Has a sense of delayed justice; being vindicated implies you faced doubt or accusation before being cleared.

examples.en: The audit completely vindicated her: every transaction had been properly authorised.
examples.es: La auditoría la vindicó por completo: todas las transacciones habían sido debidamente autorizadas.

examples.en: He felt vindicated when the technique he had championed was finally adopted industrywide.
examples.es: Se sintió vindicado cuando la técnica que él había defendido fue adoptada finalmente por todo el sector.

meaning_en: Filled with bitter hatred and extreme hostility; savagely scathing in tone.
meaning_es: Lleno de odio amargo y extrema hostilidad; de tono ferozmente virulento.
collocation: a vitriolic attack, vitriolic comments
note: Implies a sustained, intensely bitter quality beyond ordinary anger; used in criticism, politics, and online discourse.

examples.en: The vitriolic online response shocked even veterans of public debate.
examples.es: La virulenta respuesta en línea sorprendió incluso a los veteranos del debate público.

examples.en: His vitriolic column made him famous, but alienated the very politicians he needed access to.
examples.es: Su virulenta columna lo hizo famoso, pero alejó a los propios políticos a los que necesitaba tener acceso.

meaning_en: Using far more words than necessary; excessively long-winded.
meaning_es: Que usa muchas más palabras de las necesarias; excesivamente prolijo.
collocation: verbose writing, a verbose explanation
note: Critical rather than neutral; suggests the extra words obscure rather than clarify.

examples.en: The terms and conditions were so verbose that most users clicked accept without reading a word.
examples.es: Los términos y condiciones eran tan prolijos que la mayoría de los usuarios hacían clic en aceptar sin leer nada.

examples.en: Her editor returned the draft with a note: 'verbose — cut by a third'.
examples.es: Su editora devolvió el borrador con una nota: 'prolijo — recorta un tercio'.

meaning_en: Open to bribery or corruption; acting with dishonest self-interest for money.
meaning_es: Abierto al soborno o la corrupción; que actúa con deshonesto interés propio por dinero.
collocation: a venal official, venal practices
note: Specific to financial corruption rather than moral failing in general; useful in political and institutional contexts.

examples.en: The investigation uncovered a network of venal inspectors who had taken bribes for years.
examples.es: La investigación descubrió una red de inspectores venales que habían aceptado sobornos durante años.

examples.en: The playwright portrayed the court as hopelessly venal, where every favour had its price.
examples.es: El dramaturgo retrató la corte como irremediablemente venal, donde cada favor tenía su precio.

meaning_en: Relating to deep inward feelings rather than reason; powerfully instinctive and raw.
meaning_es: Relativo a sentimientos profundos e internos más que a la razón; poderosamente instintivo y crudo.
collocation: a visceral reaction, a visceral performance
note: Positive in creative contexts (visceral storytelling), neutral or negative when describing gut-level political responses.

examples.en: The film's opening sequence provoked a visceral reaction that left the audience shaken.
examples.es: La secuencia de apertura de la película provocó una reacción visceral que dejó al público sacudido.

examples.en: Her visceral dislike of the proposal had nothing to do with the budget figures.
examples.es: Su visceral rechazo a la propuesta no tenía nada que ver con las cifras presupuestarias.

meaning_en: Expressing opinions or feelings loudly and forcefully; clamorous.
meaning_es: Que expresa opiniones o sentimientos con fuerza y en voz alta; ruidoso e insistente.
collocation: vociferous critics, vociferous opposition
note: Implies volume and persistence rather than depth; a vociferous crowd or lobby is hard to ignore.

examples.en: A vociferous minority had managed to drown out the more measured majority in the consultation.
examples.es: Una minoría vociferante había conseguido ahogar a la mayoría más moderada durante la consulta.

examples.en: The decision drew vociferous protest from residents who felt bypassed by the planning process.
examples.es: La decisión provocó vociferantes protestas de vecinos que se sentían ignorados por el proceso urbanístico.

meaning_en: Accorded great respect, especially because of age, wisdom, or long-standing importance.
meaning_es: Que merece gran respeto, sobre todo por su edad, sabiduría o larga trayectoria.
collocation: a venerable institution, a venerable tradition
note: Can be used warmly or with gentle irony; 'venerable institution' sometimes implies age without adaptation.

examples.en: The venerable law firm had handled the family's affairs for four consecutive generations.
examples.es: El venerable bufete de abogados había gestionado los asuntos de la familia durante cuatro generaciones consecutivas.

examples.en: She became a venerable figure in the field, sought out for her judgement rather than her output.
examples.es: Se convirtió en una figura venerable en su campo, buscada por su criterio más que por su producción.

meaning_en: Extremely bitter or spiteful; malicious and poisonous in tone or intent.
meaning_es: Extremadamente amargo o rencoroso; malicioso y venenoso en tono o intención.
collocation: a venomous remark, venomous criticism
note: The figurative use implies the comment is designed to wound; more targeted and personal than 'vitriolic'.

examples.en: The letter was venomous in its personal attacks, going far beyond any professional criticism.
examples.es: La carta era venenosa en sus ataques personales y fue mucho más allá de cualquier crítica profesional.

examples.en: She delivered what sounded like a compliment but was, in fact, a venomous piece of sabotage.
examples.es: Pronunció lo que parecía un cumplido pero que, en realidad, era un envenenado acto de sabotaje.

meaning_en: Having or showing a feeling of vague longing or regret for something past or unattainable.
meaning_es: Con un sentimiento de vaga añoranza o nostalgia por algo pasado o inalcanzable.
collocation: a wistful smile, a wistful look
note: The longing is gentle rather than painful; a wistful tone is bittersweet, not broken.

examples.en: She gave a wistful smile when she walked past her childhood home after twenty years away.
examples.es: Esbozó una sonrisa nostálgica al pasar frente a la casa de su infancia después de veinte años de ausencia.

examples.en: He spoke wistfully about the summers before the company was sold.
examples.es: Habló con añoranza de los veranos anteriores a la venta de la empresa.

meaning_en: Using or expressing dry, ironic humour, often in the face of difficulty.
meaning_es: Que emplea o expresa un humor seco e irónico, a menudo ante las dificultades.
collocation: a wry smile, a wry observation
note: A wry smile or comment signals awareness without surprise; it suits people who cope with absurdity through understatement.

examples.en: She took a wry pleasure in the fact that her most-shared article had taken twenty minutes to write.
examples.es: Le hacía gracia, con sorna, que su artículo más compartido le hubiera llevado veinte minutos escribirlo.

examples.en: His wry account of the failed product launch became a favourite after-dinner story.
examples.es: Su irónica descripción del fracasado lanzamiento del producto se convirtió en un relato favorito de sobremesa.

meaning_en: To decrease in strength, size, or importance; to become less vigorous or intense.
meaning_es: Disminuir en fuerza, tamaño o importancia; volverse menos intenso o vigoroso.
collocation: interest waned, on the wane
note: Often used figuratively for trends, influence, or enthusiasm; the phrase 'on the wane' is a common construction.

examples.en: Public enthusiasm for the programme had waned significantly since its first series.
examples.es: El entusiasmo del público por el programa había menguado considerablemente desde la primera temporada.

examples.en: His political influence was on the wane long before he chose to step down.
examples.es: Su influencia política estaba en declive mucho antes de que decidiera retirarse.

meaning_en: Feeling or showing caution about possible dangers or problems.
meaning_es: Que siente o muestra precaución ante posibles peligros o problemas.
collocation: wary of strangers, remain wary, a wary eye
note: Describes a cautious, watchful attitude; whether the caution is warranted depends on context.

examples.en: Having been misquoted before, she was wary of journalists and chose her words with care.
examples.es: Habiendo sido malinterpretada anteriormente, desconfiaba de los periodistas y elegía sus palabras con cuidado.

examples.en: Investors remained wary despite the positive quarterly figures.
examples.es: Los inversores siguieron cautelosos a pesar de las positivas cifras trimestrales.

meaning_en: Deliberate and unprovoked; showing a complete disregard for consequences or morality.
meaning_es: Deliberado e injustificado; que muestra un total desprecio por las consecuencias o la moral.
collocation: wanton destruction, wanton cruelty
note: Implies wilfulness — the damage could have been avoided and wasn't; often used in legal and moral condemnation.

examples.en: The wanton destruction of the archive during the clearout was treated as a serious disciplinary matter.
examples.es: La destrucción deliberada del archivo durante el vaciado se trató como un grave asunto disciplinario.

examples.en: The inquiry condemned the wanton disregard for safety protocols that had led to the accident.
examples.es: La investigación condenó el deliberado desprecio por los protocolos de seguridad que había conducido al accidente.

meaning_en: Playfully quaint or odd in an amusing and appealing way; given to fanciful ideas.
meaning_es: Extravagante y curioso de forma entretenida y atractiva; dado a ideas fantásticas.
collocation: a whimsical touch, whimsical humour
note: Usually positive in creative contexts; can imply a gentle lack of seriousness when used critically.

examples.en: The children's book had a whimsical charm that appealed equally to adults reading aloud.
examples.es: El libro infantil tenía un encanto caprichoso que gustaba por igual a los adultos que lo leían en voz alta.

examples.en: Her office was full of whimsical ornaments that told visitors more about her than any CV.
examples.es: Su despacho estaba lleno de objetos caprichosos que decían más de ella que cualquier currículum.

meaning_en: Deliberate and intentional despite knowing it is wrong or undesirable; stubbornly self-willed.
meaning_es: Deliberado e intencional a pesar de saber que está mal o no es deseable; tercamente voluntarioso.
collocation: willful ignorance, willful misconduct, a willful child
note: Legal usage ('willful misconduct') and everyday usage ('willful child') share the idea of deliberateness.

examples.en: The tribunal found willful misconduct on the part of the contractor, not mere negligence.
examples.es: El tribunal declaró que la conducta del contratista fue dolosa y no una simple negligencia.

examples.en: His willful refusal to read the briefing papers frustrated everyone who had prepared them.
examples.es: Su deliberada negativa a leer los documentos de trabajo exasperó a todos los que los habían preparado.

meaning_en: In a very unhappy, unfortunate, or miserable state; of very poor quality.
meaning_es: En un estado muy infeliz, desafortunado o miserable; de muy mala calidad.
collocation: wretched conditions, feel wretched
note: Can describe people, conditions, or objects; emotional 'feel wretched' is distinct from material 'wretched poverty'.

examples.en: She felt wretched for days after the argument, unable to concentrate on anything.
examples.es: Se sintió fatal durante días tras la discusión, incapaz de concentrarse en nada.

examples.en: The documentary filmed the wretched conditions in the overcrowded transit camp.
examples.es: El documental filmó las miserables condiciones del superpoblado campo de tránsito.

meaning_en: A prolonged and complicated dispute or argument.
meaning_es: Una disputa o discusión larga y complicada.
collocation: a legal wrangle, wrangle over details
note: Implies both parties digging in; 'legal wrangle' is a very common collocation in journalism.

examples.en: The legal wrangle over the estate kept the family in conflict for nearly a decade.
examples.es: La disputa legal por la herencia mantuvo a la familia enfrentada durante casi una década.

examples.en: After months of wrangling over terms, the two studios finally signed the co-production deal.
examples.es: Tras meses de forcejeo sobre las condiciones, los dos estudios firmaron por fin el acuerdo de coproducción.

meaning_en: A person who is fanatically committed to a cause, belief, or goal, often to an extreme degree.
meaning_es: Persona fanáticamente comprometida con una causa, creencia u objetivo, a menudo de forma extrema.
collocation: a religious zealot, a zealot for reform
note: Critical in tone; implies the commitment has crossed into rigidity or intolerance of opposing views.

examples.en: He was less a reformer than a zealot, unable to accept any compromise on his vision.
examples.es: Era menos un reformador que un fanático, incapaz de aceptar ningún compromiso sobre su visión.

examples.en: The product launch attracted early zealots who evangelised it across social media.
examples.es: El lanzamiento del producto atrajo a los primeros fanáticos, que lo evangelizaron en las redes sociales.

meaning_en: The highest point reached by something; the peak of success, power, or achievement.
meaning_es: El punto más alto alcanzado por algo; la cima del éxito, el poder o los logros.
collocation: at its zenith, reach the zenith
note: Borrowed from astronomy; 'at its zenith' is a set phrase for peak influence or cultural moment.

examples.en: The studio was at its creative zenith in the mid-nineties, releasing classic after classic.
examples.es: El estudio estaba en su cénit creativo a mediados de los noventa, lanzando un clásico tras otro.

examples.en: By the time the biography was published, her reputation had passed its zenith.
examples.es: Cuando se publicó la biografía, su reputación había superado ya su punto álgido.
